title: The tensor mate at the graph-normalized unit orientation
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $f:X\to Y$ a separated quasi-compact compactifiable etale morphism between Noetherian schemes. Let $C$ be a graph/homotopy-normalized compact-support comparison family, let $\rho_f:f_A^\times\simeq Lf^*$ be its adjoint-uniqueness coordinates, and let $\eta_f:\omega_f\simeq A_X$ be their coefficient-unit component followed by the pullback-unit identification [def-pur-finite-smooth-comparison-coordinates]. For every $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, compose the inverse right unitor $f^*K\to f^*K\otimes^L A_X$, then $1\otimes\eta_f^{-1}$, then the specified projection/counit tensor map [thm-asd-smooth-tensor]. The result equals $\rho_{f,K}^{-1}$. In Lean this is finiteSmoothGammaMap A f (finiteSmoothOmegaCoordinates A C f) K = (finiteSmoothAdjointCoordinates A C f).inv.app K. No supplied geometric orientation or deformation is involved.

proof.text: Use monicity of the compactification sheaf map into direct image to identify the supplied sheaf comparison with the canonical graph normalization. Their formulas on every homotopy representative agree, so localization natural-transformation extensionality identifies their inverse derived comparisons. The existing normalizedComparison_eq_source lemma identifies this with the upstream graph comparison. The common-refinement identity law removes the selected-compactification self comparison. Expanding right-adjoint uniqueness identifies rho followed by the exact/left-derived pullback comparison with sfEtaleRightAdjointComparison.

Apply sfEtaleUnitTensorArbitraryBase to the chosen compactification and actual exceptional adjunction. Its normalized tensor equation uses exact pullback. The right-adjoint identification from the preceding step and the canonical pullback-unit comparison identify its unit morphism with finiteSmoothOmegaCoordinates.hom. Cancel the exact/left-derived pullback comparison, using tensor interchange and left-unitor naturality, to obtain theta followed by rho equal to tensoring the unit orientation followed by the left unitor.

The existing smoothTensorDualityMap_eq and ambientTensorMap_eq calculations express the specified smooth tensor map as the canonical braiding followed by theta. Insert the inverse unit orientation from finiteSmoothGammaMap. Braiding naturality moves it to the first tensor factor, where it cancels the unit orientation in the preceding equation. The braiding/unit law leaves the right unitor, which cancels its inverse. Postcomposition with the invertible rho component now gives the required equality with rho inverse.

theorem finiteSmoothOmegaTensorCoordinates
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [HasCompactification f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f] [Etale f]
    (C : FiniteSmoothCompactSupportComparisons A)
    (hC : FiniteSmoothComparisonNormalized A C)
    (K : DerivedCategoryModule A Y) :
    finiteSmoothGammaMap A f (finiteSmoothOmegaCoordinates A C f) K =
      (finiteSmoothAdjointCoordinates A C f).inv.app K
